Title: RxJava 2 and async subscriber
Description: Hi, I am using RxJava 2.1.2 and found recently sample code that worked in RxJava 1.x but seems to work differently in RxJava 2.
When I execute the code below I assume that each "subscribe" code will be run in new thread. However it is run in new but the same thread "RxNewThreadScheduler-1". I assume that Schedulers.io() should create a new thread per each long-running task. Please advice.

```java
public class SampleRx {
	public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
		Observable.fromArray("1", "2", "3")
			.observeOn(Schedulers.io())
			.subscribe(item -> { 
				System.out.println(
						Thread.currentThread().getName());
			Thread.sleep(2000); });
		Thread.sleep(7000);
	}
}
```

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about understanding the behavior of RxJava 2's thread scheduling, specifically how Schedulers.io() works compared to RxJava 1.x. The user is confused about why multiple subscriptions are running on the same thread ("RxNewThreadScheduler-1") rather than on separate threads. This is a conceptual issue about how the RxJava 2 scheduler works.

To verify the solution, we only need to understand RxJava 2's documentation and behavior, which can be done through code analysis without actually building and running the code. The solution would involve explaining that Schedulers.io() in RxJava 2 uses a thread pool rather than creating a new thread for each task, which is why the user is seeing the same thread name. This is different from RxJava 1.x behavior that the user was expecting.

This is purely a matter of understanding the API's behavior and doesn't require building or running code to verify the solution's correctness.
